component: POP3 protocol versus server UIDL interfaces

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The IDL-only patch removes nsIPop3Protocol.markMessages and its native array scaffolding. The incoming server still has a separate markMessages entry point and calls the client's direct JavaScript method with a cloned Map. That method updates UIDL status and writes state. The remaining checkMessage implementation tests UIDL-map membership, not a local-header lookup. Keep these receivers distinct; the removal does not establish a general rule against noscript APIs or remove all POP3 marking behavior.
title: Removing the protocol's native mark method leaves the server-driven UIDL path intact
